issue: Does a prior state drug conviction count as a 'controlled substance offense' under U.S.S.G. § 4B1.2(b) when the substance is controlled under state law but not under the federal Controlled Substances Act?

sides.position: 'Controlled substance' in § 4B1.2(b) refers to the federal definition, so a state conviction involving a substance not federally controlled does not qualify.
cases: United States v. Townsend, 897 F.3d 66 (2d Cir. 2018)

sides.position: 'Controlled substance' in § 4B1.2(b) is not limited to federally controlled substances, so a state drug conviction can qualify under the state-law approach.
cases: United States v. Sheffey, 2020 WL 3495944 (6th Cir. June 29, 2020)
United States v. Whitfield, 726 F. App'x 373 (6th Cir. 2018)

quote: We recognize that a circuit split exists on this issue, and that the weight of authority favors Ruth.
cite: United States v. Nathaniel Ruth, 966 F.3d 642 (7th Cir. 2020)
